novelty_claim: Evolves the parent's single-word masking into full-intent fragmentation: an auxiliary LLM masker selects EVERY intent-bearing content word (action verb + key objects), each rendered as its own ASCII-art block, so the visible plaintext retains only function words and carries no harmful semantics; the victim decodes the art blocks and reassembles the instruction itself.
initial_hypothesis: Masking all intent-bearing content words (LLM-selected, each rendered as ASCII art) instead of one dataset word removes the plaintext intent that drives the consensus refusal mode, converting refusals into decode-and-comply trajectories and lifting mean ASR well above the locked 0.000 baseline across the 4-victim panel, at 1 victim call per goal (parent used 2).
key_insight: Census of the locked baseline's 600 trajectories (published-leaderboard, 0.000 ASR on the frozen 50): the dominant consensus failure (66-83% per victim) is direct refusal driven by the PLAINTEXT remainder of the instruction — masking one dataset-category word leaves intent fully visible (e.g. 'commit identity theft and evade [MASK]'). The single masked word hides a token, not the intent.
